correctness.rationale: In a deletion-minimal word any chosen pair of embeddings covers all positions, or an uncovered position could be deleted. Each symbol therefore occurs once or twice. Put C=1...n-1. A single zero forces C on each side with no extra positions, hence C0C, whose two required embeddings are unique. For two zeros, A can always reuse the first instead of a later zero, and B can always reuse the last instead of an earlier zero. If a nonzero symbol j occurs just once, both embeddings must pass through it. The prefix required by A through the cut contains the prefix required by B, so one A-prefix embedding can serve both: minimality forces the left part to equal 0...j-1. The symmetric right requirement is the longer B suffix j+1...n-1,0. Thus the only such word is 0C0, with each position essential. All other candidates have every symbol twice and hence length 2n. The exhibited E_n has a unique embedding of A: its earlier zero and all second copies of nonzero letters are forced in forward order. B must use its later zero and all first copies in reverse forcing order. These embeddings are disjoint and exhaustive for n>=3, proving minimality and attainability, not a classification of every full-length word. For n=2, a word containing both 01 and 10 has at least three runs and therefore contains 010 or 101; minimality gives precisely those two. Inspected RESULT.md lines 23–43, verify.py, VERIFICATION.md and verification_output.txt. The bundled Python 3 alignment enumeration and separate small direct search are finite corroboration, not required for the proof; their recorded outputs were read and not re-executed.
